The two major streaming platforms slated to merge, HBO Max and Paramount+, may ultimately fail to come together.

After Netflix withdrew from the bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery, the relevant plans were announced in March of this year. However, a federal judge has now issued a temporary restraining order, blocking the deal from being completed for at least the time being...

The original merger plan

Once the deal is completed, Paramount will acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, and its streaming platforms HBO Max and Paramount+ will be integrated into a single service.

Temporary restraining order

Audiences reacted coolly to the plan, worried it would weaken competition and lead to price hikes. A coalition of 12 state attorneys general shared the same concern and petitioned a federal court to issue a temporary restraining order to block the deal. According to NBC News, the court has now approved the request.

The temporary restraining order is valid for 14 days, during which the court will hold hearings. Even if Paramount wins the case, the merger plan is also under review by the European Union and UK governments. The Writers Guild of America has also filed an antitrust lawsuit, arguing that the merger would lead to job losses and lower pay.
